Analysis by Richard Cowan 

(MarijuanaNews note: As readers may have observed, I was not entirely overly impressed by the American College of Physicians report on medical marijuana, but it would never have occurred to me to lie about it. 

See 

Party Like It’s 1999! American College of Physicians Bases Its Endorsement of Medical Marijuana on 1999 IOM Report, Sponsored by Drug Czar, and Czar’s Office Says It Is “A Political Act.” 

But that may be why I could not be the editorial page editor of the Tacoma News Tribune. When I read their editorial this Sunday, I decided to wait a day before I responded. It’s Tuesday, but I still don’t understand why someone who does not work for the DEA or the Drug Czar’s office (where lying is fundamental part of the job) would write something so completely dishonest. 

To give them the benefit of the doubt, perhaps they did not actually read the ACP report . 

There was no link to it on their website, and that it typical of prohibitionists, who prefer to give their interpretation of what “the opposition” is saying. Indeed, prohibitionists almost never link to anti-prohibitionist sites or quote us at length.  


I have observed that whenever people with closed minds (AKA bigots) are confronted with something that threatens their biases, they look for some rescue by their “authority.” So, perhaps they called up the Drug Czar’s office or some other prohibitionist propaganda organization and asked them for a few factoids and quotes they could take devoid of context. 

See 

Reuters Madness and the Subordination of Journalism to Prohibitionist Propaganda. Conning CNN. Lies Lead to Wars, But Then, That Is Their Purpose. 

At first, I considered writing a “Letter to the Editor”, but it would not be possible to do the subject justice in that format. There are simply too many problems – lies – to cover. And whatever their motives, they really did violate the Commandment against giving false evidence against their neighbors.) 

Smoking is healthy? THE NEWS TRIBUNE 

February 23rd, 2008

Well, no, smoking isn’t actually healthy. But the American College of Physicians – an association of internists – recently decided that smoking marijuana is therapeutic, right? 

(MarijuanaNews note: Recently?? As the title of my comment on the ACP report indicates, it was based largely on the 1999 Institute of Medicine Report. Incomprehensibly, there is no mention of the IOM in the editorial, which is one reason that I doubted that the editor actually read the ACP report.) 

See 

Executive Summary Of The IOM Report, Marijuana And Medicine: Assessing The Science Base 

Well, no, smoking isn’t actually healthy. But the American College of Physicians – an association of internists – recently decided that smoking marijuana is therapeutic, right? 

Not quite. We need to draw a crucial distinction here. What a lot of people don’t get – and other people try to obscure – is that the real argument about medical marijuana is about delivery, not content. 

(MarijuanaNews note: Not quite, indeed. First, there is still much that is unknown about the medical effect of the various ingredients in whole cannabis. Second, neither the IOM nor the ACP reports completely rejected “smoking” as a method of delivery. Now I find  myself wondering if they even read their own editorial, because just below, they quote the ACP: “Although the long-term effects of smoked marijuana may not be relevant for patients with terminal illnesses or debilitating symptoms…” 

The second reason that I wondered if they read the ACP report was that it placed so much emphasis on vaporization, even mentioning the Volcano brand by name, because it was used in a study in San Francisco. If “the real argument about medical marijuana is about delivery,” then the argument should be over.) 

One guy who apparently doesn’t get it is the writer of the Los Angeles Times article on the College’s position paper. 

(MarijuanaNews note: That would be Eric Bailey. ) 

The story dwelt on marijuana advocates’ glee that the ACP had joined their cause. It accurately noted the ACP’s (accurate) conclusion that some of the chemicals in cannabis had medicinal value. But it left out a small detail: The College pointedly rejected the smoking of marijuana. 

(MarijuanaNews note: Now I wonder if the Tacoma editor actually read the LA Times story. Bailey wrote, “The ACP position paper urges the use of NON-SMOKED (emphasis added, so that even an editor can see it) forms of cannabis as well as further research to identify the illnesses best treated with cannabis and the proper dosages for specific conditions.” 

Bailey also reported, “An FDA spokeswoman declined to comment on the group's position and referred inquiries to a 2006 media advisory noting that the agency has never approved of smoked marijuana as a medical treatment.” And Bailey included the link to the FDA, but then he is a real journalist, not a lying hack.) 

Take this excerpt, for example: 

“The chronic effects of smoked marijuana are of much greater concern, as its gas and tar phases contain many of the same compounds as tobacco smoke. Chronic use of smoked marijuana is associated with increased risk of cancer, lung damage, bacterial pneumonia, and poor pregnancy outcomes.”

See 

Annotated NORML Weekly News for February 7, 2008; NORML Responds to “Latest Research”. Cannabinoids Kill Cancer. Noting Obama’s Retreat. 

and 

Johns Hopkins Study Finds No Link Between Marijuana Use and Head, Neck, or Lung Cancer. There Was Also No Link Between This Study and Media Coverage.

Also: “Although the long-term effects of smoked marijuana may not be relevant for patients with terminal illnesses or debilitating symptoms, the residual effects of smoked marijuana are prohibitive for long-term medical use.” In other words, you don’t get healthy by smoking bud. Sorry to spoil the party, dudes. 

(MarijuanaNews note: Dudes?? Get a grip! This is not a party. It is about arresting sick and dying Americans because of the venomous lies told by generations of self-important, semi-literate hacks who cannot or will not even read the material they think that the are critiquing. If the publishers of the Tacoma paper had any decency, they would assign 

this editor to the obituary section where he could write about other brain dead stiffs.)

See 

Canadian Supreme Court Hearings Could Make History, But They Are Only Good For A Joke In DEAland Media. Filed Under Oddly Enough. Dude, Is This Journalism? 

What the ACP actually advocates is the development of pure, precisely dosed pharmaceuticals – not smoke from burning leaves – that deliver the medically useful compounds in cannabis like, well, real medicine. 

(MarijuanaNews note: Well, real medicine is something that helps patients, not just something that appeals to the biases of dishonest editors. Here is what the ACP said, “The development of a vapor route for THC delivery offers promise for the future of medical marijuana research. A recent study found that THC administered through the Volcano® vaporizer resulted in higher plasma THC levels than smoked marijuana at both 30 and 60 minutes after administration. It also found that exhaled carbon monoxide increased very little after vapor compared with smoking (37). Those findings,

along with patient preference for the vapor method, indicate opportunities for future clinical trials. Vaporization of THC offers the rapid onset of symptom relief without the negative effects from smoking. It allows patients to selfregulate their dosage immediately by ceasing inhalation when or if psychoactive effects become unpleasant. Scientists are also developing a pulmonary dronabinol to be delivered with a pressurized metered-dosed inhaler. Preliminary studies show rapid absorption, but FDA approval remains distant.” (emphasis added) 

See 

Vaporizing Cannabis and the Prohibitionist Party Line. The AMA Wants the Government to Invent the Vaporizer! A New Index Page. 

And since the dope-smoking lobby is cherry-picking from this report, let’s pick a couple cherries of our own: 

(MarijuanaNews note: The “dope-smoking lobby”?) 

From Annotated NORML Weekly News for February 22, 2008 Mourning Dr. Morgan, More On American College Of Physicians, More or Less Democracy in Idaho? : “With this action, the ACP joins the American Nurses Association, the American Public Health Association, the American Academy of Family Physicians, and many other medical associations calling for cannabis to be made a legal medicine.” 

• In “medical marijuana” states like Washington, marijuana cigarettes are sometimes recommended for chronic conditions (see “chronic effects” above). 

(MarijuanaNews note: Why the quotation marks around “medical marijuana”, when the editorial previously said, “the real argument about medical marijuana is about delivery, not content.” And why does it say “marijuana cigarettes”? Oh, I keep forgetting, no medicine is smoked.) 

These include glaucoma and epilepsy. But the ACP is highly skeptical of marijuana’s much-touted power to treat these conditions. 

See 

Eye Specialist On Board of Florida Prohibitionist Propaganda Organization Opposes Medical Marijuana for Glaucoma. But Inspires No Faith In His Profession. 

and links 

• The high-inducing tetrahydracannabinol (THC) in marijuana does relieve pain at lower doses. But it intensifies sensitivity to pain at higher doses – another good reason for controlled doses. 

(MarijuanaNews note: Controlled dosing – titration – is important in any medication, but inhalation of smoke or “vapor” is actually the best way to control dosage, because it produces the most rapid effect.) 

See 

More Arresting Developments. Record Marijuana Arrests Go Unreported. “No

Medicine Is Smoked” – So DEA Busts Edibles Maker. 

The ACP does fall in with High Times in calling for the federal government not to threaten doctors or patients with prosecution in states that allow medical marijuana. 

(MarijuanaNews note: No, they fell in with the APA, and as for arresting doctors, the Supreme Court of the US, in the Conant case.) 

See 

One Cheer for the American Psychiatric Association, Pending Approval of Their Call to Stop Arresting Their Medical Marijuana Patients. 

The problem here is that criminal drug-dealing syndicates have been concealing themselves among good faith medical marijuana operations.

See 

Program notes for the MarijuanaNews World Report July 7, 2005 UK Report: “two years ago and a lot has happened since then.” Dutch Crime Down. US Script Abuse Up. Narks On Online Seeds. No Pot Candy? 

and 

T’was Another Great Victory. Teen Marijuana Use Down; Oxy Use Up. Teen Cigarette Use Went Down More Than Teen Marijuana Use. 

and 

Florida Governor Demonstrates Absurdity of War on Cannabis. Prescription Drugs Kill; Cannabis Does Not – So The Killers Are “Just As Detrimental” As Cannabis .
On the science, the College is dead on. On the realities of law enforcement, maybe not so much. 

See 

California Narks Lie to Justify Disobeying Prop 215. And They Lie About Me In The Process.
